Except where otherwise noted, all currency amounts are stated in United States dollars.


**Financial and Production Highlights**


- Net income attributable to Methanex shareholders of $265 million, Adjusted EBITDA of $543 million, and Adjusted net income of $284 million in the third quarter.
- Reported an average realized price in the third quarter of $510 per tonne compared to $529 per tonne in the second quarter of 2026. Based on our October and November posted prices and current spot pricing, we expect that our average realized price range will be approximately $525 to $550 per tonne for these two months.
- Produced 2,143,000 tonnes of methanol in the third quarter, with record North American production.
- Announced an agreement to sell substantially all of our remaining New Zealand natural gas contractual entitlements commencing in the first quarter of 2027 and continuing through the end of the decade when such entitlements expire. The expected indefinite idling of our New Zealand production facilities during the first quarter of 2027 resulted in a $10 million accrual for restructuring activities, which has been included as a deduction in the calculation of Adjusted EBITDA.
- Generated $646 million of cash flows from operating activities, returned $14 million to shareholders through regular dividends and ended the quarter with $912 million in cash. Provided notice to redeem $300 million of our existing $700 million bonds due in October 2027 and expect to redeem the final $400 million during the fourth quarter of 2026.
- Subsequent to the quarter, announced approval of a 5% normal course issuer bid to repurchase up to 3,868,213 common shares through November 3, 2027.


VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Oct. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — For the third quarter of 2026, Methanex (TSX:MX) (NASDAQ:MEOH) reported net income attributable to Methanex shareholders of $265 million ($3.42 net income per common share on a diluted basis) compared to a net income of $198 million ($2.45 net income per common share on a diluted basis) in the second quarter of 2026. Adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 was $543 million and Adjusted net income was $284 million ($3.69 Adjusted net income per common share). This compares with Adjusted EBITDA of $577 million and Adjusted net income of $300 million ($3.87 Adjusted net income per common share) for the second quarter of 2026.


Rich Sumner, President & CEO of Methanex, said, “The Middle East conflict’s dramatic impact on the methanol industry persisted through the third quarter, with the significant loss of industry supply supporting ongoing pricing strength. Our enhanced asset base continued to run well, particularly in North America, helping to drive another quarter of strong Adjusted EBITDA and cash flow. We remain focused on operating our assets and supply chain safely and reliably as we continue to navigate dynamic conditions.”


FURTHER INFORMATION


The information set forth in this news release summarizes Methanex’s key financial and operational data for the third quarter of 2026. It is not a complete source of information for readers and is not in any way a substitute for reading the third quarter 2026 Management’s Discussion and Analysis (“MD&A”) dated October 29, 2026 and the unaudited condensed consolidated interim financial statements for the period ended September 30, 2026, both of which are available from the Investor Relations section of our website at[www.methanex.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=VBfYVrw00mxn3mKKs6eS3JJNpyCsI26d7n1Wtl9OWSgZzqhjwQd-iPfNJMr1lJK9ajAtoG8Djbpww33q3JjBDEyvQBuL1dEUpYukSCiBp74=) . 1. The asset impairment charge includes $26 million ($33 million, net of tax) relating to the Titan facility and the Company’s 63.1% share of the impairment charge recognized by Atlas of $74 million ($82 million, net of tax).


- We recorded net income attributable to Methanex shareholders of $265 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to net income of $198 million in the second quarter of 2026. Net income in the third quarter of 2026 was higher compared to the prior quarter primarily due to the impact of the asset impairment charge recorded in the second quarter of 2026. This was partially offset by a lower average realized price in the third quarter of 2026.
- We sold 2,595,000 tonnes of methanol in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 2,555,000 tonnes of methanol in the second quarter of 2026. Sales of Methanex-produced methanol were 2,279,000 tonnes in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 2,151,000 tonnes in the second quarter of 2026.
- Production of methanol for the third quarter of 2026 was 2,143,000 tonnes compared to 2,213,000 tonnes for the second quarter of 2026. Production was strong across our North American and Egypt assets and was lower in Chile, where we experienced expected seasonal gas availability constraints. In Trinidad, production declined as the Titan plant ceased operations and was indefinitely idled.
- We announced an agreement to sell substantially all of our remaining New Zealand natural gas contractual entitlements commencing in the first quarter of 2027 and continuing through the end of the decade when such entitlements expire. The expected indefinite idling of our New Zealand production facilities during the first quarter of 2027 resulted in a $10 million accrual for restructuring activities, which has been included as a deduction in the calculation of Adjusted EBITDA.
- In the third quarter of 2026 we paid a quarterly dividend of $0.185 per common share for a total of $14 million.
- At September 30, 2026, we had a strong liquidity position, including a cash balance of $912 million and access to a $400 million unutilized revolving credit facility. The Company provided notice to redeem $300 million of our existing $700 million bonds originally due in October 2027. The amount was repaid subsequent to the quarter.
- Subsequent to the quarter, on October 29, 2026, we announced approval of a 5% normal course issuer bid to repurchase up to 3,868,213 common shares through November 3, 2027.

Key production and operational highlights during the third quarter include:


**United States**


Geismar produced 1,007,000 tonnes in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 1,027,000 tonnes in the second quarter of 2026. Beaumont produced 199,000 tonnes of methanol and 83,000 tonnes of ammonia in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 185,000 tonnes of methanol and 83,000 tonnes of ammonia in the second quarter of 2026. Beaumont’s methanol production was higher as the plant was offline for approximately 30 days starting in early June to repair the cooling tower. The Natgasoline plant produced 221,000 tonnes of methanol (Methanex share) in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 204,000 tonnes of methanol (Methanex share) in the second quarter of 2026.


**Canada**


Medicine Hat produced 140,000 tonnes in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 143,000 tonnes in the second quarter of 2026.


**Chile**


Chile produced 221,000 tonnes in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 322,000 tonnes in the second quarter of 2026. Production was lower in the third quarter compared to the second quarter as we undertook a single-plant operation through most of the period due to the seasonal reduction of gas availability from Argentina. We restarted two-plant operations late in September. We have gas contracts in place with Chilean and Argentinean gas producers until 2030 and 2027, respectively, which underpin approximately 55% of the site’s gas requirements year-round. While seasonality in production is expected to continue, we are seeing generally positive developments in natural gas availability to supply our Chile facilities.


**Egypt**


Egypt produced 330,000 tonnes (Methanex interest – 165,000 tonnes) in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 330,000 tonnes (Methanex interest – 165,000 tonnes) in the second quarter of 2026. Gas availability in Egypt is influenced by several factors, including domestic production levels, gas imports and seasonal demand fluctuations. We are monitoring the gas market closely and we may experience curtailments in the future, particularly in the summer months, depending on gas supply and demand dynamics in the domestic and international markets.


**New Zealand**


New Zealand produced 156,000 tonnes in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 46,000 tonnes in the second quarter of 2026. Production was higher in the third quarter due to a planned winter outage in the second quarter to supply gas to the New Zealand electricity sector. The plant was restarted in July and continues to operate at reduced rates. We announced an agreement to sell substantially all of our remaining New Zealand natural gas contractual entitlements commencing in the first quarter of 2027 and continuing through the end of the decade when such entitlements expire, and the expected indefinite idling of the New Zealand production facilities during the first quarter of 2027.


**Trinidad**


In Trinidad, the Titan plant produced 34,000 tonnes in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 121,000 tonnes in the second quarter of 2026. Production was lower in the third quarter as the plant ceased operations and was indefinitely idled.


**Outlook**


We expect our 2026 production to be approximately 9.0 million tonnes (Methanex interest) of methanol and 0.3 million tonnes of ammonia. Actual production may vary by quarter based on gas availability, turnarounds, unplanned outages and unanticipated events.


Based on our October and November posted prices and current spot pricing, we expect that our average realized price range will be approximately $525 to $550 per tonne for these two months. Based on a higher realized price and similar sales of produced methanol, we are expecting higher Adjusted EBITDA in the fourth quarter.
